youtube.title: The Government Predicted Katrina a Year Early | Hurricane Pam
youtube.description:
In July 2004, FEMA funded a week-long exercise in Baton Rouge built around a fictional storm, "Hurricane Pam", hitting New Orleans. It projected floodwater more than 10 feet deep, more than a million people evacuated, hundreds of thousands of buildings destroyed and more than 60,000 deaths. Follow-up planning stalled; former FEMA director Michael Brown said "money was not available to do the follow-up." Thirteen months later, Hurricane Katrina hit, levees and floodwalls failed in more than 50 places, and about 80% of New Orleans flooded. In 2006 the Army Corps of Engineers acknowledged problems with the design.

📂 Case File #056: Hurricane Pam

Sources: CBS News / AP, "Simulation Predicted Storm's Havoc" https://www.cbsnews.com/news/simulation-predicted-storms-havoc ; SourceWatch, "Hurricane Pam" simulation https://sourcewatch.org/index.php/%22Hurricane_Pam%22_simulation ; "2005 levee failures in Greater New Orleans" (Wikipedia and its citations).
